# B2B Decision Makers & Work Email Finder from Public Sources

Build a B2B prospect list from the open web instead of a rented contact database. This actor reads public company team, leadership and about pages, Wikidata, SEC EDGAR filings, UK Companies House, GitHub organizations and public LinkedIn guest/search surfaces. It normalizes every person into a searchable lead with title, seniority, department, location and company context. It never asks for a login, cookie, API key or paid data plan.

Work-email handling is evidence-first. An address is emitted as `workEmail` only when it is published on a public page (status `valid`) or when a generated pattern candidate passes MX + SMTP checks (`valid` or `catch-all`). Pattern candidates that could not be mailbox-verified remain in `emailCandidates` with their pattern and confidence, so nothing is presented as a verified address when it is only a guess.

## What you can do

| Mode | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `companyLeads` | Give one or more company domains or names and get their public decision makers and employees. |
| `search` | Filter by job title, seniority, department, industry, size, country, region, city, keywords or company. Without a company, Wikidata shortlists matching companies and LinkedIn search surfaces matching public profiles. |
| `personLookup` | Resolve a name plus a company domain or name to public profiles and email-pattern candidates. |
| `profileLookup` | Paste public `linkedin.com/in/` URLs (bulk/CSV-friendly) and enrich them with public profile data. |
| `emailLookup` | Give work email addresses and resolve the company domain, public identity (including Gravatar when present) and mailbox status. |
| `fromUrl` | Paste an Apollo people-search URL or a LinkedIn Sales Navigator lead-search URL. Its filters are parsed and run on public sources without an account or seat. |

## Sources and what each contributes

- **Company website** — leadership, team, management, about, contact and press pages; JSON-LD Person/Organization, microdata, staff cards, photos, published emails and phones.
- **Wikidata** — company industry, headquarters, size, official site, key people, founders, board members and their photos/LinkedIn IDs.
- **SEC EDGAR** — officers and directors from recent Forms 3/4/5 and proxy statements, plus ticker, CIK, SIC industry and headquarters for US registrants.
- **UK Companies House** — company profile and current/former officer appointments, role, nationality and country of residence.
- **GitHub** — organization members, public profiles and public push events that expose author name/email pairs for pattern evidence.
- **LinkedIn via public search** — DuckDuckGo Lite results for `site:linkedin.com/in` queries; no login or cookie is used.
- **LinkedIn guest profiles** — public profile pages for name, headline, location, photo, employer and education. LinkedIn returns HTTP 999 to ordinary clients, so the actor first requests the same public page through standard link-preview crawler user agents.
- **Gravatar** — public profile lookup for an email hash in `emailLookup` mode.

## Input reference

| Input | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `companyLeads` | `search`, `companyLeads`, `personLookup`, `profileLookup`, `emailLookup` or `fromUrl`. |
| `jobTitles` | – | Any title or synonym phrase. |
| `seniorities` | – | Normalized seniority multi-select. |
| `departments` | – | Normalized department multi-select. |
| `companyNames` | – | Resolved to a public website. |
| `pastCompanies` | – | Keep people whose public profile lists one of these employers. |
| `companyDomains` | – | Primary company input for `companyLeads`. |
| `excludeCompanyDomains` | – | Drop these domains. |
| `excludeJobTitles` | – | Drop titles or headlines containing any phrase. |
| `industries` | – | Industry filter and Wikidata shortlist. |
| `companySizes` | – | Employee band multi-select. |
| `countries` | – | Country names or ISO codes. |
| `regions` | – | States, provinces or regions. |
| `cities` | – | City names. |
| `locations` | – | Free-text location strings. |
| `keywords` | – | Every keyword must appear. |
| `searchQuery` | – | Extra keyword convenience field. |
| `names` | – | Names for `personLookup`. |
| `profileUrls` | – | Public LinkedIn profile URLs. |
| `emails` | – | Email addresses for `emailLookup`. |
| `sourceUrl` | – | Apollo or Sales Navigator URL for `fromUrl`. |
| `maxLeads` | 25 | Hard result cap, 1-1000. |
| `maxPerCompany` | 10 | Per-company cap, 1-200. |
| `maxPagesPerCompany` | 8 | Website pages read per company, 1-30. |
| `dataSources` | – | Any of website, wikidata, sec, companiesHouse, github, linkedinSearch, linkedinProfiles. |
| `verifyEmails` | true | Try MX/SMTP on pattern candidates; published addresses are always evidence. |
| `requireEmail` | false | Drop leads without a valid, catch-all or published email. |
| `includePhones` | false | Add published phone numbers. |
| `includePersonalEmails` | false | Add published free-mail addresses. |
| `includeCompanySummary` | true | Write per-company counts to the run summary. |

## Input examples

Company leads:

```json
{
  "mode": "companyLeads",
  "companyDomains": ["hubspot.com", "monzo.com"],
  "seniorities": ["founder", "c_level", "vp", "director", "head"],
  "maxLeads": 50,
  "maxPerCompany": 15,
  "includeCompanySummary": true
}
```

Title search with a location:

```json
{
  "mode": "search",
  "jobTitles": ["Head of Sales", "VP Revenue"],
  "locations": ["London, United Kingdom"],
  "companySizes": ["51-200", "201-500"],
  "maxLeads": 100
}
```

Apollo or Sales Navigator URL:

```json
{
  "mode": "fromUrl",
  "sourceUrl": "https://app.apollo.io/#/people?personTitles[]=CTO&personLocations[]=Germany&organizationDomains[]=stripe.com"
}
```

## Output fields

Each dataset row is one person:

`fullName`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `headline`, `jobTitle`, `seniority`, `department`, `city`, `region`, `country`, `location`, `profileUrl`, `photoUrl`, `companyName`, `companyDomain`, `companyLinkedinUrl`, `companyIndustry`, `companySize`, `companyHq`, `companyTicker`, `companyWikidataId`, `companyCik`, `companyNumber`, `companyDescription`, `workEmail`, `emailStatus`, `emailConfidence`, `emailPattern`, `emailEvidence`, `emailSourceUrl`, `emailCandidates`, `phones`, `personalEmails`, `sources`, `sourceUrls`, `firstSeenDate`, `scrapedAt`, `dataQuality`.

The run summary in the key-value store adds per-company counts (`peopleFound`, `emailsVerified`, `catchAllEmails`, `leadsWithCandidates`, inferred pattern and evidence addresses), filters used, ignored URL filters and the limitations that applied.

## Email status meanings

- `valid` — published on a public page or accepted by the mailbox server; `emailEvidence` says which.
- `catch-all` — the domain accepts random recipients, so the address is deliverable but not person-confirmed.
- `unverifiable` — MX exists but SMTP is unavailable from the run egress. This appears only for a user-supplied address in `emailLookup`.
- `invalid` — no mail exchanger.
- `unverified-pattern` — candidate only; kept in `emailCandidates`, never promoted to `workEmail`.

## Practical notes

- The default prefill is a two-lead HubSpot run over its public team pages, Wikidata and its public LinkedIn company page. It is intentionally the cheapest run that still returns records.
- `maxPagesPerCompany` controls website depth. More pages means better team coverage and more email-pattern evidence, but a longer run.
- `requireEmail` is strict: a lead without a valid, catch-all or published work email is dropped.
- Seniority and department come from the public title. When a GitHub member has no title, the department is inferred as engineering and flagged in `dataQuality`.
- Company size is normalized to an employee band when the source gives a range.
- Every URL in `sourceUrls` is a public source reference; `emailCandidates` always cite the pattern and confidence.
- No user credentials, cookies, proxy configuration or third-party enrichment API is required.

## Known limits

- Public sources cover leadership, board and technical teams unevenly. Some companies publish no team page at all.
- LinkedIn guest pages can throttle or return an auth wall; the actor first retries through link-preview crawler user agents, then falls back to public search snippets, and keeps the record only when a public identity is present.
- SMTP port 25 is blocked on some Apify cloud egress. In that case the actor still resolves MX records and published addresses, but it cannot mailbox-verify a generated candidate on that run.
- A company must publish at least one name/email pair (or a GitHub commit email) before a personal pattern can be inferred. Role addresses such as `sales@` do not reveal a personal pattern.
- Email lookup returns the public identity attached to an address, not the contents of a mailbox. Private mailboxes stay private.
- Search engines and social networks change their anti-bot behavior; the actor records what it could fetch and never fabricates a missing field.

## FAQ

**Is this a scraped contact database?** No. It is a live research actor: every run reads public pages and public records, then de-duplicates and normalizes the result.

**Does it need an Apollo or LinkedIn account?** No. `fromUrl` only parses the filters in the URL you paste; the search runs on public sources.

**Why do some leads have no email?** Because no public address matched the person and no pattern could be inferred or verified. The record still contains the identity, company and source trail, and any pattern candidates appear under `emailCandidates`.

**What happens to role addresses?** They are treated as company contact addresses, not as a person's work email.
